source.place: ## Proof, Step 6: 'it is Frobenius-equivariant because both operators are those of Step 5', asserted without argument; cf. Deligne, La conjecture de Weil I (literature/deligne-weil-I_PMIHES-1974-43.pdf), (1.3) p. 274 ('Pour X propre, les deux coincident') and (1.12) p. 278

proof.text: *Step 1 (finite coefficients).* Use the identity compactification fixed in the statement. By [def-weil-extension-by-zero], for $j=\operatorname{id}_Y$ every object factors through $j$, so $P_M=M$ and $j_!M=M$, on objects and morphisms. Thus [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed] gives $Ra_{Y!,n}=Ra_{Y*,n}$; the proper comparison $\kappa$ of [prop-weil-proper-compact-coincidence] is this identification. In [lem-trf-open-square-exchange] put $U'=Y'=U=Y$ and $j'=j=\operatorname{id}_Y$. Its restriction-to-$U'$ clause now says that the entire open-square map $b_{g_Y}$ is the identity under the pullback identifications. Consequently the two arrows defining $\operatorname{FrEx}_{Y,!}$ in [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange] (2) are $\operatorname{FrEx}_{Y,*}(M)$ followed by $Ra_{Y*}(\operatorname{id})$. This proves clause 1 at $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$, including the specified identifications $Lg_s^*\kappa_M$ on the source and $\kappa_{Lg_Y^*M}$ on the target.

*Step 2 (integral and field coefficients).* Use the same identity compactification at every level. The formulas in [def-weil-derived-direct-image] and [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] give the same strict coefficient tower for $Ra_{Y!}M$ and $Ra_{Y*}M$: at level $m$ both are $\operatorname{Res}_mRa_{Y*,m}(M\otimes^L A_{E,m})$, with the same quotient-induced transitions. Indeed, [lem-sf-compact-support-restriction-of-scalars] specifies the compact-support restriction comparison as the direct-image restriction comparison composed with $j_!\operatorname{Res}=\operatorname{Res}j_!$; for $j=\operatorname{id}$ the latter identification is the identity. On the simultaneous section models of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], extension by zero along the identity is the identity functor, with identity adjunction unit and counit. Its open-adjunction mate $b$ is therefore the identity system map. In the notation of [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange], $\mathcal J_{\operatorname{id}}=\operatorname{id}$, $p=a_Y$, and $e_{a_Y}^{c}=\mathcal F_{a_Y}(\operatorname{id})\circ e_{a_Y}=e_{a_Y}$ as system maps. Under $\kappa$, the canonical comparisons $\alpha_!,\beta_!$ in that definition are $\alpha_*,\beta_*$: their source and target system operations and their defining units and counits coincide. Thus the two integral exchange composites are the same $\beta_*\circ\mathcal L_s(e_{a_Y})\circ\alpha_*$, proving clause 1 for $\mathcal O_E$. Applying the scalar-localization functor to this equality proves it for $E$; representing an object and these equal morphisms at a common finite field stage proves it for $\Qlb$, exactly as prescribed in [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange]. This uses equality of specified system maps before $R\varprojlim$, rather than inferring equality from their finite evaluations.

*Step 3 (point complexes).* Write $F=\operatorname{Fib}_s$, $G=Lg_s^*$, $N_!=Ra_{Y!}M$, $N_*=Ra_{Y*}M$, and $M'=Lg_Y^*M$. Naturality of the point transport [lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural] (2), applied to $\kappa_M:N_!\to N_*$, says $\iota_{N_*}\circ F(\kappa_M)=F(G\kappa_M)\circ\iota_{N_!}$. Clause 1 and functoriality of $F$ [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] now give
$$
\begin{aligned}
\tau_M\circ F(\kappa_M)
&=F(\operatorname{FrEx}_{Y,*}(M))\circ\iota_{N_*}\circ F(\kappa_M)\\
&=F(\operatorname{FrEx}_{Y,*}(M))\circ F(G\kappa_M)\circ\iota_{N_!}\\
&=F(\kappa_{M'})\circ F(\operatorname{FrEx}_{Y,!}(M))\circ\iota_{N_!}\\
&=F(\kappa_{M'})\circ\tau_{c,M}.
\end{aligned}
$$
The first and last equalities are the two transport composites of [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport]. Their source and target are the cohomology complexes of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology]. This is clause 2 at the complex level.

*Step 4 (cohomology).* Applying $\mathrm H^i$ to the point-complex equality of Step 3 gives, for every integer $i$, $\mathrm H^i(\tau_M)\circ\mathrm H^i(\operatorname{Fib}_s\kappa_M)=\mathrm H^i(\operatorname{Fib}_s\kappa_{Lg_Y^*M})\circ\mathrm H^i(\tau_{c,M})$ on $H_c^i(Y,M)$, using the definitions of ordinary and compact-support cohomology in [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] and preservation of composition by the cohomology functor.

tool_uses.why: The proper-case step uses its stated identification Ra_{Y!} \cong Ra_{Y*} to identify the comparison \kappa with the identity compactification comparison; this generic proper comparison is supplied outside the finiteness unit.
The chosen compactification formula uses the normalized open-exchange map; the whole open is Y here.
The existing exchange definition uses simultaneous system adjunction maps; setting the open immersion to the identity gives its identity mate before inverse limit.
The transport definition separates this generic naturality assertion from its construction; clause 2 is applied to the proper comparison morphism.
Its specified composite becomes the ordinary direct-image scalar restriction comparison for the identity open, proving that the two actual coefficient towers have equal transition maps.

split_report.statement_correction: The compactification used for the exchange was implicit; it is now explicitly the identity compactification already fixed for kappa. The source proper-case assertion and its use by prop-cohomological-finiteness are unchanged.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q84-416ef0963 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all 13 cited node statements (the blueprint_update statements are identical to the current ones), unit sk-lem-finite, the citer prop-cohomological-finiteness Step 4, the current blueprint main-20261015 Step 6 ('Frobenius-equivariant because both operators are those of Step 5', which it asserts without argument), and Deligne Weil I (1.3) p.274 ('Pour X propre, les deux coincident') and (1.12) p.278. Hypotheses check out: proper implies separated finite type, so the transport and compact-support definitions apply. kappa is the specified identification for the identity compactification that the proof of prop-weil-proper-compact-coincidence constructs, not just an isomorphism that exists. The statement now says FrEx_! uses the same identity compactification. This only makes explicit a choice that def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange (2) already treats as part of the construction. It is recorded and is not a weakening. Step 1: with j=id the sheafification of P_M=M is canonically M. lem-trf-open-square-exchange's restriction-to-U' clause on the whole open gives b=id, and naturality of FrEx_* reduces clause 1 to that normalization, which I checked by hand. Step 2: the towers are the same, and the transitions agree through the composite named in lem-sf-compact-support-restriction-of-scalars. J_id=id and b=id on the lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections models, so e^c=e and alpha_!,beta_! equal alpha_*,beta_*. E is handled by localization and Qbar by common-stage classes; no rational object is reduced. Step 3: the naturality in lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural (2) gives the correct 4-line chain, with domains and targets matching. Step 4 is functoriality of H^i. Edge cases (empty Y, M=0, Y_0=Spec k_0, n=1, all i) need no exceptions. There are no new nodes. An rg search of dag/nodes found no duplicate and no cycle; the only citer is the ancestor. No SGA is cited.
